FunAsrNet.description: Explore Mandarin speech AI in pure C#: recognition, synthesis, browser transcription, and telephone audio processing.
features: Mandarin ASR, VAD segmentation, and WebSocket transcription
Chinese speech synthesis and browser demos
CPU SIMD and an explicitly enabled Vulkan hybrid backend
FunAsrNet.note: An independent community implementation, not an official FunASR SDK. Compatible model weights must be prepared separately. No NuGet package has been published.
FunAsrNet.overview: FunASR.NET brings model loading, audio features, neural-network operators, VAD, and Mandarin synthesis into a familiar .NET stack. CLI tools, a web service, and browser demos offer a path from transcribing one recording to experimenting with interactive speech applications.
scenarios: Explore Mandarin transcription and speech output in .NET apps
Experiment with browser microphones, WebSockets, and VAD segmentation
Work with PCM, G.711, and resampling in telephone-audio experiments
requirements: Install the matching .NET 10 SDK specified in the README
Prepare and verify compatible model weights separately
The optional Vulkan backend requires a compatible system driver
steps: Clone the source, build the solution, and run the checks that do not require models.
Prepare the ASR / VAD or Mandarin TTS weights using the model documentation.
Choose the CLI or web-service example and validate it with your own audio.

SimdYolo.eyebrow: Give your code a new perspective
SimdYolo.description: Pure C# YOLO inference and detection-head fine-tuning, with object detection, instance segmentation, and pose estimation.
features: Load supported PT and ONNX model files directly
Object detection, instance segmentation, and pose estimation
CPU SIMD, Vulkan / Metal backends, and detection-head fine-tuning
SimdYolo.note: Model and operator support is limited to the repository's compatibility list. Metal has not been validated on real hardware. Training fine-tunes the detection head with a frozen backbone. Current source: 0.11.3; formal Release: 0.11.2. Check startup optimizations and deployment instructions against the version you use.
SimdYolo.overview: SimdYolo implements YOLO inference and supported detection-head fine-tuning in pure C#. It reads supported PT and ONNX files, uses SIMD / intrinsics on the CPU, and offers Vulkan and Metal backends. The repository includes a web example, model documentation, and reproducible validation reports. The current source is 0.11.3 while the formal Release is 0.11.2. Source changes optimize loading, first inference, workspace reuse and Vulkan instance reuse, with an optional ReadyToRun fast-start deployment. These source changes are not part of the 0.11.2 downloads.
scenarios: Explore detection, segmentation, and pose in .NET image applications
Study model loading and execution without a Python inference runtime
Experiment with labeling, pre-labeling, and supported detection-head fine-tuning
requirements: A .NET 10 SDK or a matching runtime
Supported weights and tasks, with model licenses reviewed
Compatible GPU drivers when using a GPU backend; validation differs by backend
steps: Install the inference package or build from source.
Prepare weights from the supported model list and read the inference examples.
Validate a single image before exploring the web demo or fine-tuning workflow.

PureDb.eyebrow: Keep data close to your code
PureDb.description: A pure .NET 10 embedded file database. Candidate 1.0.0-rc.1 adds SQL, JSON, ADO.NET, transactions and consistent backups, with large-database and checkpoint improvements.
features: KV / SQL, composite indexes, CTEs, window functions and C# user functions
Transactions, savepoints, multi-threaded writes and consistent backups
rc.1 large-range access, checkpoint improvements and optional SQLite file compatibility
PureDb.note: 1.0.0-rc.1 is a release candidate. SQL and SQLite file compatibility have explicit limits; full SQLite SQL and the WAL file protocol are not supported. Assess performance, memory and production suitability with your own workload.
PureDb.overview: PureDb implements an embedded file database with C# and the .NET 10 standard library. Neither its core nor its optional SQLite file-compatibility package needs third-party NuGet or native libraries. Candidate 1.0.0-rc.1 provides KV, SQL, JOINs, JSON, composite indexes, foreign keys, CTEs, window functions, transactions and ADO.NET. This update focuses on large primary-key ranges, checkpoint memory reclamation, range mutations and consistent backups. Consult the SQL support list and candidate reports for limits and measured results.
scenarios: Explore embedded storage for local tools and desktop apps
Query structured and JSON data through SQL or ADO.NET
Study managed database internals, transactions, and file compatibility
requirements: A .NET 10 development environment
Check SQL, transaction and concurrency boundaries for candidate 1.0.0-rc.1
Review file-compatibility limits and back up SQLite files before use
steps: Install PureDb 1.0.0-rc.1; KV and SQL APIs use separate files.
Start with parameterized queries and transactions, then explore C# user functions and backups.
Use the same version for SQLite compatibility and evaluate scale, recovery and memory using the rc.1 reports.

SimdSkia.description: An independent C# 2D engine. Stable 0.1.1 integrates with Avalonia 12.1.x desktops, using CPU SIMD and optional Vulkan / Direct2D backends.
features: Stable 0.1.1, verified with Avalonia 12.1.0–12.1.5
Windows, Linux X11 and macOS desktop integration with Native AOT validation
C# drawing, fonts, image codecs and optional Vulkan / Direct2D
SimdSkia.note: 0.1.1 is a stable patch for the documented feature subset. It does not promise complete SkiaSharp APIs, binary replacement or pixel-equivalent output. macOS GPU / Metal is not implemented; future Avalonia versions need further validation.
SimdSkia.overview: SimdSkia implements 2D drawing, fonts, basic text layout and image codecs in C#. Stable patch 0.1.1 compiles its adapter against Avalonia 12.1.0 and verifies the same binary with 12.1.0–12.1.5. Desktop packages select companion hosts for the application version. CPU rendering is the default, with optional Windows Direct2D or Windows / Linux Vulkan. The repository documents real-window and Native AOT validation across three platforms.
scenarios: Study C# graphics, glyph rendering, and pixel compositing
Evaluate rendering backends in Avalonia desktop examples
Compare startup, allocation, memory, and visual quality in specific workloads
requirements: .NET 10 for applications; SDK 10.0.403+ to build the repository
Keep Avalonia packages on one version; 12.1.0–12.1.5 are verified and 13.x is outside the supported range
Linux needs X11 / XWayland; macOS uses the official native window host; GPU backends need compatible drivers
steps: Install SimdSkia.Avalonia.Desktop 0.1.1 and align all directly referenced SimdSkia.* packages.
Configure UseSimdSkiaDesktop() and adjust existing rendering-backend references as documented.
Optionally install the matching GPU package, then assess real pages for fonts, quality, performance and memory using the compatibility reports.

Serein.description: A pure .NET streaming engine for RTSP/RTP ingestion, media remuxing, live distribution, and recording.
features: RTSP / RTP / MPEG-PS media ingestion
RTSP, HTTP-FLV, and WebSocket-FLV output
Recording, managed audio processing, and ASP.NET Core integration
Serein.note: A preview focused on unpacking and forwarding video, not general video transcoding. HLS and WebRTC output are not implemented.
Serein.overview: Serein focuses on ingesting, unpacking, remuxing, distributing, and recording media. Unified media frames and MediaStreamHub connect RTSP / RTP inputs to RTSP, HTTP-FLV, WebSocket-FLV, and file outputs, with managed .NET code and ASP.NET Core integration. The video pipeline primarily handles packaging and forwarding.
scenarios: Explore RTSP ingestion and multi-subscriber distribution in .NET services
Build HTTP-FLV / WebSocket-FLV playback and recording experiments
Study RTP / PS processing, resampling, and media-status events
requirements: A .NET 10 SDK or matching application runtime
An accessible RTSP source, or start with the no-source example
Verify that your required output protocol is supported
steps: Install the ASP.NET Core integration package or build the source examples.
Run the sample service and inspect its read-only status API.
Configure your media source locally and validate distribution and recording.

yunsevo.title: Yunsevo Drive
yunsevo.description: .NET cloud file management and cross-platform synchronization, with permissions, version history, resumable transfers, and desktop / Android clients.
features: User and group permissions, quotas, version history, and recycle bin
Chunked resumable transfers, multi-directory sync, and auditing
Windows / Linux / macOS and Android clients
yunsevo.note: Choose the platform and architecture specified in Releases. No iPhone installation package is currently available.
yunsevo.overview: Yunsevo combines a .NET cloud file service with cross-platform sync clients. It covers user and group permissions, quotas, version history, a recycle bin, and auditing. Transfers support resumable chunks; desktop clients handle multiple servers and directories, while Android provides file and photo workflows.
scenarios: Evaluate privately deployed file management and team-folder permissions
Explore multi-directory synchronization across desktop platforms
Manage engineering photos and files with the Android client
requirements: Complete packages matching your platform and architecture
Persistent server storage and the first-install setup wizard
Read migration notes and back up data and configuration before upgrading
steps: Download the server and client packages from Releases and read their instructions.
Run the server and configure administrator access and storage in the setup wizard.
Sign in with a personal account, create a sync task, and verify permissions and recovery.

p2pvpn.description: An independent virtual-networking project with network and device management, P2P hole punching, clients, and separate relay nodes.
features: Network, group, and device management
P2P direct connections with optional WSS relays
Windows and Linux clients, plus Android source
p2pvpn.note: Connectivity depends on NAT, firewalls, and network conditions. Relaying requires deployed online nodes. Platform availability follows the current release documentation.
p2pvpn.overview: P2P VPN includes a public website, a user console, clients, backup hole-punching nodes, and independent relays. Users manage networks, groups, and devices, with clients preferring direct connections. The control service coordinates accounts and connectivity; relaying depends on deployed online infrastructure.
scenarios: Validate virtual-network connections between grouped devices in a controlled environment
Study NAT traversal, control coordination, and optional relaying
Evaluate client behavior across operating systems and network conditions
requirements: Check the current release for operating-system and architecture support
Configure server authentication, email, and nodes as documented
Client installation and virtual interfaces require appropriate system permissions
steps: Read the deployment and architecture documents to understand each service's role.
Create a network and group in your test environment, then add devices.
Verify connectivity with a second grouped device and evaluate relay needs.

ProtoBus.description: A .NET multi-transport, multi-protocol communication framework aimed at industrial, IoT, and vehicle connectivity.
features: TCP / UDP / serial / Unix sockets / CAN transport directions
MQTT, SIP, GB28181, and JT/T 808 protocol directions
Industrial protocol directions including Modbus, FINS, and S7
ProtoBus.note: The public README is currently brief. These are the repository's stated directions; inspect the source for actual implementation, examples, and availability.
ProtoBus.overview: ProtoBus is described as a unified .NET communication framework across transports and protocols for industrial, IoT, and vehicle systems. The README lists TCP, UDP, serial, Unix sockets, CAN, MQTT, SIP, and Modbus among its directions. Public documentation is currently brief, so implementation details must be verified in the source.
scenarios: Understand a multi-transport communication framework's intended structure
Study industrial, IoT, and vehicle protocol-integration requirements
Evaluate implementation against a specific device or protocol experiment
requirements: Inspect the current source, project structure, and build requirements
Prepare appropriate test devices or protocol simulators
A protocol name alone does not establish complete or production-ready support
steps: Clone the repository and inspect its current implementation and structure.
Confirm the status of your required transport and protocol, then review available examples.
Test with your own device or simulator and use Issues for clarification.

SimdPaddleOCR.title: SimdPaddleOCR
SimdPaddleOCR.eyebrow: Read the text inside your images
SimdPaddleOCR.description: Pure C# PP-OCRv6 inference with a managed ONNX interpreter and SIMD kernels for detection, orientation, and recognition.
features: Text detection, orientation classification, and recognition
Managed ONNX interpretation and SIMD kernels
Pixel-memory input and optional GPU backends
SimdPaddleOCR.note: Maintained by sdcb. The core accepts pixel memory rather than decoding images. Optional GPU paths require .NET 10 and compatible Vulkan or Metal drivers; consult the repository for supported models and platforms.
SimdPaddleOCR.overview: SimdPaddleOCR provides managed OCR with a pixel-memory API, allowing callers to choose their image decoder and prepare the documented models. Public NuGet packages provide core functionality and model components.
scenarios: Extract text from images and documents in .NET
Study managed ONNX and SIMD inference
Compare pixel-layout and image-decoder integration
requirements: Prepare .NET, models, and image decoding as documented
Verify supported formats, models, and GPU backends
steps: Install the core package and documented model packages.
Supply pixel memory following an example and validate your images.

PaddleSharp.description: .NET/C# bindings for Paddle Inference and PaddleOCR, with OCR, detection, table recognition, and model tooling.
features: .NET bindings for the Paddle Inference C API
OCR, table recognition, and supported detection models
Platform-specific CPU / GPU runtime packages
PaddleSharp.note: This wraps native Paddle Inference and requires matching platform, architecture, and runtime packages. It is not a native-dependency-free C# inference engine.
PaddleSharp.overview: PaddleSharp brings Paddle Inference and related model workflows into .NET. Its repository documents OCR, detection, orientation, Chinese segmentation, and model conversion. Choose packages, models, and runtimes for the specific task.
scenarios: Integrate OCR and table recognition into .NET document workflows
Evaluate Paddle models across CPU / GPU environments
Explore Chinese text and image-model integration
requirements: A compatible .NET environment, native runtime, and models
Matching CUDA and drivers for GPU packages
steps: Choose task-specific core, model, and runtime packages using the documentation.
Start with a minimal example and validate your own images and environment.

chats.eyebrow: A workspace for multiple AI models
chats.description: A .NET LLM frontend and AI gateway connecting model providers through conversations, multimodal workflows, tools, and administration.
features: Multiple model providers and compatible API protocols
Conversation, image, and optional tool workflows
Docker / native deployment and user management
chats.note: Capabilities, pricing, and availability depend on your model providers and configuration. Optional code-execution tools require the documented runtime setup.
chats.overview: Sdcb Chats combines a multi-model frontend with an AI gateway. It offers conversation UI, API protocols, storage choices, and management features. Choose Docker or a native package and configure the providers you need.
scenarios: Evaluate conversations and multimodal capabilities across model providers
Explore a self-hosted AI frontend and API gateway
Test tool workflows and management in your own environment
requirements: Docker or a matching native release as documented
Your own model-provider, storage, and optional tool configuration
steps: Choose your database and runtime using the deployment documentation.
Configure providers and validate users, conversations, and tools.

OpenVINO.NET.description: High-quality .NET bindings for OpenVINO inference, with device selection, OpenCvSharp extensions, and OCR components.
features: .NET interfaces for the OpenVINO C API
Platform runtime packages and device inference
OpenCvSharp extensions and PaddleOCR components
OpenVINO.NET.note: Use native runtime packages matching the version, platform, and architecture. Device and model support follows OpenVINO and repository documentation.
OpenVINO.NET.overview: OpenVINO.NET provides .NET interfaces and extensions around the OpenVINO inference toolkit. It helps C# applications load models, prepare inputs, and execute inference, with platform runtimes, OCR components, and YOLO examples.
scenarios: Evaluate OpenVINO inference in .NET apps
Connect OpenCvSharp processing to model inference
Explore supported devices, platforms, and models
requirements: A compatible .NET environment and matching native runtime
Supported models, devices, and drivers
steps: Choose the core interface and matching platform runtime.
Load a model using an example and validate your real device and inputs.

Sdcb.FFmpeg.description: FFmpeg bindings and higher-level wrappers for C#/.NET, including media contexts, codec interfaces, filters, and frame helpers.
features: Generated low-level FFmpeg interfaces
Wrappers including FormatContext and CodecContext
Filter and video-frame helpers
Sdcb.FFmpeg.note: Matching native FFmpeg libraries are required. This work evolved from FFmpeg.AutoGen; review both project and FFmpeg-build licensing when distributing applications.
Sdcb.FFmpeg.overview: Sdcb.FFmpeg brings FFmpeg interfaces to .NET with higher-level C# wrappers. Its documentation explains generation, versioned packages, and native-runtime selection.
scenarios: Study media I/O and codec workflows in .NET
Build filter and frame-processing experiments
Integrate existing FFmpeg tooling with C# apps
requirements: Native FFmpeg libraries matching your version and architecture
Review API examples and relevant distribution licenses
steps: Choose your FFmpeg version and matching interface/runtime packages.
Validate input, output, and resource cleanup with a repository example.

Arithmetic.description: A pure managed C# arithmetic library with BigInt, BigRational, correctly rounded Real, and .NET generic-math integration.
features: Arbitrary-precision BigInt, BigRational and correctly rounded Real
1.2.2 validates explicit precision consistently across public Real APIs
Fixes for large exponents, RootN degrees, bit indices and shift counts
Arithmetic.note: Pure managed version 1.2.2 is published. Invalid explicit Real precision now throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Historical GMP/MPFR bindings live in a separate repository; assess numerical behavior and performance for your workload.
Arithmetic.overview: Sdcb.Arithmetic supplies BigInt, BigRational, and Real types for arbitrary precision, correct rounding, and portable execution. The repository includes generic-math integration and hardware-specific paths. Version 1.2.2 validates explicit precision on every public Real API: 0 selects the default; other values must be in [2, int.MaxValue / 64], otherwise ArgumentOutOfRangeException is thrown. It also includes preceding fixes for large exponents, RootN degrees, bit indices and shift-count truncation.
scenarios: Study high-precision integer, rational, and floating-point arithmetic
Use arbitrary-precision types in generic-math code
Compare precision and hardware execution paths
requirements: A compatible .NET environment as specified in the README
Appropriate number types, precision, and rounding modes
steps: Install Sdcb.Arithmetic and read the type documentation.
Validate precision, boundaries, and resource needs with small examples.

SimdCodecs.description: Pure managed .NET image codecs by sdcb, covering JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, GIF and more, with SIMD acceleration and NativeAOT support.
features: Multi-format image I/O including JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF and GIF
AVX2, SSE, ARM AdvSimd and scalar fallback, without native codec libraries
Optional HEIF / HEIC decoding in 1.4.0, plus EXIF / ICC processing
SimdCodecs.note: The published NuGet version is 1.4.0; encoding and decoding support varies by format. HEIF / HEIC requires a separately installed and registered extension; MIT does not grant HEVC patent rights. Version 1.x outputs 10-bit HEIC as 8-bit samples and does not support AVIF. Main-branch 2.0 APIs differ from 1.x.
SimdCodecs.overview: Maintained by sdcb, SimdCodecs implements image codecs in pure C# for .NET 10, without native codec dependencies and with NativeAOT compatibility. Its facade identifies formats from file headers and decodes pixels into caller-owned buffers. Individual codecs support formats including JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF and GIF, with EXIF / ICC processing; JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 provide decoding. Version 1.4.0 adds separately installed and registered HEIF / HEIC support. Benchmark results depend on the hardware, corpus and measurement conditions documented in the repository.
scenarios: Build image-loading, conversion and thumbnail workflows in .NET services
Provide RGB / BGRA / grayscale buffers to OCR, computer vision or desktop rendering
Evaluate managed decoding in NativeAOT or WebAssembly environments
requirements: A .NET 10 environment and the APIs documented for published version 1.4.0
SIMD selects AVX2 / SSE / AdvSimd where available, with a scalar fallback
HEIF / HEIC needs Sdcb.SimdCodecs.Heif and explicit registration; review format and patent notes
steps: Install Sdcb.SimdCodecs 1.4.0 and inspect image headers with TryReadInfo.
Follow the 1.4.0 README to allocate a buffer and call TryDecodeIntoRgba8 or an explicit pixel-format API.
Choose the encoder for your format; for HEIC, install the extension and call SimdCodecs.Register(HeifImageDecoder.Registration).
